ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the central atom is carbon, connected respectively to Br on the left, Br below, Br above, and PPh3 on the right; a positive charge is marked near PPh3, indicating the phosphonium center. In the upper right of the image there is a free Br bearing a negative charge. A curved arrow shows the electron pair of this Br− pointing to the upper Br connected to the central carbon; another curved arrow shows the bond electrons of the central carbon and the upper Br returning to carbon. Reasoning: Therefore, free Br− combines with the upper Br to generate BrBr; the original C–Br bond breaks, and the bond electrons remain on carbon, making the central carbon negatively charged. The remaining structure is carbon still connected to two Br and positively charged PPh3. The corresponding SMILES is Br[C-]([P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3)Br.BrBr.

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: identify C bonded to left Br, bottom Br, top Br, and PPh3+, with separate Br−. Apply the arrows: Br− bonds to the top bromine, while the C–top-Br bond electrons move to carbon. Thus the top bromine leaves carbon and combines with Br− to form BrBr, and the carbon retains bonds to two Br atoms and PPh3+ while gaining a negative charge. Encode that state as Br[C-]([P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3)Br.BrBr.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image to determine the unchanged framework: the product must still contain PPh3+ attached to the central carbon and two bromines attached to that carbon. The reacting external Br− pairs with the departing upper bromine, so those two bromine atoms become molecular bromine, BrBr. Since the C–Br bond electrons remain on carbon when that bromine departs and phosphorus is still [P+], the carbon is [C-]. Therefore write the ionic ylide fragment as Br[C-]([P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3)Br and append the separate Br2 molecule with a dot.
